What Is the Universal Snipping Tool Shortcut?

The primary Snipping Tool shortcut across modern Windows versions is Windows Key + Shift + S. Pressing these three keys together dims your monitor instantly and opens the top screen-capture overlay, allowing you to snip rectangular areas, freehand shapes, individual app windows, or your entire screen directly to the clipboard.

This hotkey works right out of the box on Windows 10 and Windows 11 without opening a separate program window first. Your captured image automatically copies to your system clipboard, ready for instant pasting into emails, documents, or chat apps.

How to Open Snipping Tool With Keyboard Shortcut and Modes

Learning how to open Snipping Tool with keyboard shortcut combinations unlocks four distinct capture profiles. When you press Windows Key + Shift + S, a slim control bar appears at the very top of your display.

The first option is Rectangular Snip, which lets you drag a box around any specific visual element. The second is Freeform Snip, letting you draw custom, irregular outlines around anything on your desktop.

The third icon triggers Window Snip, which highlights individual open program windows so you can capture an app cleanly without background clutter. The fourth icon is Fullscreen Snip, which instantly takes an image of your entire workspace across all active monitors.

Once you make a selection, Windows saves the file temporarily to your clipboard and generates an interactive banner in your notification center. Clicking that pop-up opens the full Snipping Tool editor where you can crop, annotate, or run optical character recognition on text.

Windows 11 Snipping Tool Shortcut Key and New Features

The Windows 11 Snipping Tool shortcut key brings expanded functionality that goes far beyond simple static captures. Microsoft merged the legacy legacy tool with Snip & Sketch, building native screen recording directly into the app.

To switch to video capture, open the tool interface directly or toggle the camera icon at the top of the app window. You can record video clips with system audio and microphone inputs without installing third-party utilities.

The Windows 11 release also includes an automated Text Actions engine. This tool detects written words inside your screenshots, allowing you to extract raw text or redact sensitive data like phone numbers and email addresses with one click.

Audio recording settings can be adjusted inside the tool before you start recording. This makes quick software walkthroughs, bug reports, and short presentations remarkably fast to produce.

How to Capture Screen Using Snipping Tool Shortcut Options

  • Windows Key + Shift + S: Opens the modern Snipping Tool selection bar for targeted, full, or custom screen regions.
